title: Thermodynamics

sections.title: Thermodynamic State Variables, Internal Energy, and the First Law
sections.pedagogical_purpose: Define thermodynamic equilibrium, establish internal energy U as an exact state function, and formulate the First Law of Thermodynamics dQ = dU + dW using consistent physics sign conventions.
unresolved_gaps: No standalone canonical question atoms or worked examples for First Law sign convention and PV work integration in current staging.
Missing questions distinguishing chemistry vs physics sign conventions for work.

sections.title: Standard Gas Processes and Work on PV Diagrams
sections.pedagogical_purpose: Systematize isobaric, isochoric, and isothermal processes, calculating boundary work from integral P dV and analyzing closed indicator diagrams.
source_references: University Physics with Modern Physics, 13th Edition.pdf
unresolved_gaps: Missing approved formula records for isothermal work (W = n R T ln(V2/V1)) and isobaric heat capacities (Cp, Cv, Mayer's relation) in ChapterSpec.
No verified question atoms for cyclic PV processes staged in current KB.

sections.title: Reversible Adiabatic Processes in Classical Ideal Gases
sections.pedagogical_purpose: Derive and apply reversible adiabatic scaling relations T V^(gamma-1) = const and P V^gamma = const, compute boundary work, and resolve sign misconceptions regarding internal energy variation.

sections.title: Radiation Thermodynamics and Photon Gas Adiabatic Expansion
sections.pedagogical_purpose: Extend thermodynamics beyond classical non-relativistic matter to relativistic blackbody radiation, deriving u = a T^4, radiation pressure P = u/3, and adiabatic scaling T V^(1/3) = const.
source_references: Feynman, Richard P. The Feynman Lectures on Physics.pdf
unresolved_gaps: Missing dedicated step-by-step worked example demonstrating the derivation of T R = constant from d(uV) + P dV = 0.

sections.title: Heat Engines, the Carnot Cycle, and Second Law Formulations
sections.pedagogical_purpose: Analyze thermal cycles, calculate theoretical engine efficiency eta = 1 - T_C / T_H, and examine Kelvin-Planck and Clausius statements of the Second Law.
source_references: University Physics with Modern Physics, 13th Edition.pdf
unresolved_gaps: Topic 'heat-engines-and-second-law' has no approved concept records, formula records, or question atoms in current ChapterSpec.
Need canonical atoms for Carnot cycle and refrigerator coefficient of performance (COP).

pedagogical_synthesis_notes: Thermodynamics Template: Structured around the First Law as the foundational energy-accounting framework, branching into classical ideal gas adiabatic transitions and advanced radiation pressure extensions.

Misconception Neutralization: Section 3 directly targets misc-td-01 (conflation of adiabatic work signs with temperature change), ensuring students grasp that compression work done ON the gas increases internal energy and elevates temperature.

Modern Extension and Rigor: Section 4 bridges classical thermodynamics to relativistic and quantum physics by demonstrating how the First Law applies to photon gases where energy density is a function of temperature alone (u = a T^4), shattering the false generalization of PV^(5/3) = const (misc-td-02).
unresolved_gaps: Gap in Topic 'first-law-and-processes': Subtopics 'isothermal-process' and 'pv-diagrams-and-work' lack approved formula records and question atoms in ChapterSpec.
Gap in Topic 'special-thermodynamic-processes': Lacks a canonical worked example for the adiabatic expansion of photon gas cavity.
Gap in Topic 'heat-engines-and-second-law': Zero canonical questions, formulas, or worked examples for Carnot efficiency and refrigerator COP.
